steps.title: A — Acidosis
steps.body: Severe metabolic acidosis (pH <7.1–7.2) refractory to medical therapy warrants urgent dialysis.
steps.tip: Bicarbonate alone is insufficient when anion gap is rising despite treatment.

steps.title: E — Electrolytes
steps.body: Refractory hyperkalemia with ECG changes despite medical management is a classic emergent indication.
steps.tip: Repeat calcium and insulin/D50 while preparing dialysis.

steps.title: I — Intoxication
steps.body: Dialyzable toxins: methanol, ethylene glycol, lithium, salicylates, and some alcohols.
steps.tip: Consult poison control and nephrology early.

steps.title: O — Overload
steps.body: Pulmonary edema refractory to diuretics and oxygen/ventilation requires fluid removal via dialysis.
steps.tip: UF rate should be cautious in hypotensive patients.

steps.title: U — Uremia
steps.body: Uremic encephalopathy, pericarditis, or intractable nausea/vomiting from uremia are indications — not BUN number alone.
steps.tip: Bleeding diathesis from uremia also supports urgent RRT.
